summary: A minimal blog with Bear's constitution: Markdown in, static HTML out, zero client-side JavaScript and one stylesheet under 5 KB. Tags, RSS, a sitemap, optional privacy analytics, and a custom domain. Everything you add is a reason it stops being Bear.

stack.choice: One Node script with markdown-it, pinned

stack.why: the constraint that makes it Bear

stack.choice: Any static host on your domain

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: Your existing posts as Markdown
prerequisites.get: Bear: Dashboard > Settings > Export. Otherwise copy your posts into Markdown files with a date.

prerequisites.name: A static host
prerequisites.get: Cloudflare Pages, Netlify or GitHub Pages connected to the repo.

prerequisites.name: A domain or subdomain
prerequisites.why: The point of leaving is a domain you own.
prerequisites.get: Register at Cloudflare Registrar, Porkbun or Namecheap, or use a subdomain of one you already own. You add one DNS record in the deploy phase.
prerequisites.cost: roughly $10 a year, or free on an existing domain

env.name: SITE_URL
env.where: Canonical base for RSS and OG.

phases.title: Build pipeline
phases.goal: posts/*.md to dist/, drafts excluded, frontmatter errors loud.

steps.detail: Read posts/*.md with frontmatter (title, date, slug, tags, draft), render index.html newest first and one page per post, copy static assets.
commands: mkdir bear && cd bear && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module && npm install markdown-it@14 gray-matter@4

steps.do: Fail the build on a missing title or date, naming the file

check: Adding a post and rebuilding adds it to the list

phases.title: The stylesheet
phases.goal: Under 5 KB, inlined, no script tag anywhere.

steps.do: Write styles.css: measured line length, system fonts, dark mode via prefers-color-scheme, readable code blocks
Add a build check that fails if the CSS exceeds 5 KB or any script tag appears in dist/

check: The built stylesheet is under 5 KB
The page ships no script tag

phases.title: Tags and RSS
phases.goal: Tag pages, a full-content feed, sitemap, robots.

steps.do: Render feed.xml with full content, sitemap.xml and robots.txt

check: Every tag page lists only its posts

phases.title: Privacy analytics (optional)
phases.goal: Pageviews without a cookie or a raw IP, or nothing at all.

steps.do: Decide: read the host's logs, or add one tiny endpoint
steps.detail: The endpoint logs a daily-salted hash of IP and user agent per path; /stats behind basic auth. Write the decision down.

steps.do: If you add the endpoint, keep the page's zero-JavaScript rule by using a 1x1 image request, not a script

check: Pageviews for today match the day's rows
Still no script tag in the HTML

phases.title: Deploy
phases.goal: One command from Markdown to live.

steps.do: Connect the host and the custom domain
Write the README with the zero-JavaScript constitution and how to add a post in three lines

check: A new post goes from file to live with one command

phases.title: Keep it Bear
phases.goal: Guardrails so the blog stays small as it grows.

steps.do: Add a CI check that fails on any script tag, any external request, or CSS over 5 KB
Add a size budget for HTML per page and an accessibility audit in CI

check: A commit adding a script tag fails CI
A commit growing CSS past 5 KB fails CI

product.outcome: A blog whose constraints are enforced by the build, so it stays fast and private for years.

architecture.swap: Any generator that passes the same checks

notIncluded: The Bear discover feed; it is the community.
after: An email-me-new-posts option via RSS-to-email you do not run
